target.title: fix(matrix): reject non-canonical synthetic thread cursors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix threaded message reads could mistake non-canonical variants of OpenClaw's synthetic thread-start cursor for the cursor OpenClaw actually issued. Appended junk, base64url padding, or extra JSON fields were silently treated as the internal first-page marker instead of being forwarded as opaque Matrix pagination tokens.

## Why This Change Was Made

Synthetic cursors are now recognized only when both the base64url payload and the complete decoded envelope exactly round-trip to OpenClaw's canonical encoder output. Matrix homeserver `nextBatch` and `prevBatch` values remain opaque and are not canonicalized. Risk is limited to rejecting aliases of an OpenClaw-owned marker; the production-path proof covers both canonical marker handling and opaque-token forwarding.

## User Impact

Matrix threaded reads no longer silently restart relation pagination when given a malformed or structurally altered synthetic cursor. Canonical cursors emitted by OpenClaw continue to start the next relation page normally.

## Evidence

On Node v24.18.0, I drove the real exported `readMatrixMessages()` function. The only substitute was the Matrix network client, used to capture the exact `from` token passed to the Matrix SDK.

Before, using the unmodified `upstream/main` production file with the same harness, all three non-canonical values were swallowed as the internal marker:

```text
canonical: from=undefined
appended-junk: from=undefined
padding-alias: from=undefined
extra-field: from=undefined
node-base64url-premise: true
```

The `node-base64url-premise: true` line independently confirms that Node's base64url decoder accepts the appended-junk payload and decodes it back to the canonical bytes.

After the fix, the canonical marker still maps to no Matrix token, while every non-canonical value is forwarded unchanged:

```text
canonical: from=undefined
appended-junk: from="openclaw.matrix.thread-relations-start:eyJ2IjoxLCJ0aHJlYWRJZCI6IiR0aHJlYWQtcm9vdCJ9!"
padding-alias: from="openclaw.matrix.thread-relations-start:eyJ2IjoxLCJ0aHJlYWRJZCI6IiR0aHJlYWQtcm9vdCJ9="
extra-field: from="openclaw.matrix.thread-relations-start:eyJ2IjoxLCJ0aHJlYWRJZCI6IiR0aHJlYWQtcm9vdCIsImV4dHJhIjp0cnVlfQ"
node-base64url-premise: true
```

The focused regression test fails in all three new cases against `upstream/main` and passes after the fix:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/matrix/src/matrix/actions/messages.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       17 passed (17)
```

Also run: targeted `oxfmt`, `git diff --check`, and Codex autoreview (`patch is correct`, confidence 0.97, no actionable findings). No live Matrix homeserver round-trip was run; the affected branch is fully exercised before network I/O by capturing the real production function's Matrix SDK arguments.

AI-assisted: Codex helped implement and review the change; the production-path proof and focused tests were run manually.
